verifier_a.independent_derivation_or_calculation: Audited from first principles: Rotating disc with crawling insect example verified. Disc mass M, radius R; insect mass m = M/2, moving from r = 0 to r = R. Moment of inertia: I_disc = (1/2)*M*R^2; insect at r contributes m*r^2 = (1/2)*M*r^2 => I(r) = (1/2)*M*(R^2 + r^2). Conservation of angular momentum under tau_ext = 0 gives L_z = I_0*omega_0 = (1/2)*M*R^2*omega_0 = constant. Angular velocity function: omega(r) = I_0*omega_0 / I(r) = (R^2 / (R^2 + r^2))*omega_0. At rim r = R: omega(R) = (R^2 / (2*R^2))*omega_0 = omega_0 / 2. Rotational kinetic energy ratio: K_rot(R) / K_rot(0) = (L^2 / (2*I_f)) / (L^2 / (2*I_0)) = I_0 / I_f = ((1/2)*M*R^2) / (M*R^2) = 1/2. Physical loss of 50% mechanical energy explained via negative work done by transverse Coriolis force and muscular energy absorption. Dimensional homogeneity: [omega] = rad/s, [K_rot] = J, ratio is dimensionless. Limiting cases audited: r -> 0 yields omega_0; m -> 0 yields omega_0; domega/dr < 0 monotonic. All calculations verified.
